description: Chief Science Officer @ Sereact 🦾 Chief Science Officer (m/f/d) · Zurich or Stuttgart, Boston possible · Reports to the CEO · Full-time Who we are Sereact builds the robot brain for physical work. Cortex, our vision-language-action foundation model, is hardware-agnostic: the same model runs single-arm and dual-arm systems, mobile manipulators and humanoids that pick, sort and handle returns in live production across Europe and the US. Customers include Zalando, IKEA, BMW, Rohlik and DHL. Founded in 2021 in Stuttgart, with an R&D hub in Zurich and a US office in Boston. We have raised more than $145 million, most recently a $116 million Series B led by Headline, with Zalando as a strategic investor. We work in small, senior teams with a flat structure; execution counts more than titles. Why this role, why now Our robots produce data no lab can stage. Our fleet has recorded more than 500 million manipulation interactions in live warehouse operations; Cortex 2.0 was trained on a curated 10 million of them and added a world model that plans before it acts (arXiv 2604.20246). Cortex 2.5 learns a new task from a few demonstrations instead of a training run. Deployments are growing from single robots to fleets, and the research team is growing with them. We now want one scientific leader who owns the research behind Cortex end to end and turns what our fleet experiences every day into the next step change in what robots can do. The Real-World Learning Loop is your system Sereact is a frontier research lab and a production-grade robotics company in one. Our bet: general-purpose robotic intelligence “must be learned from live deployments” (The Real-World Learning Loop, Feb 2026). Every stage of that loop is yours to raise: In-Situ Policy Execution. Every robot in production runs the current policy, and every shift is an experiment. You decide what the policies expose for learning. Continuous Data Acquisition. Robots annotate their own interactions while they work. You decide what is worth recording and which situations the fleet should go and find. Data Curation and Learning. Novelty, uncertainty, failures and distribution shift decide what we learn from. You own the curation and the training recipe. Evaluation and Policy Redeployment. Updated policies pass validation gates before they return to the fleet. You set the bar, and how fast we can clear it safely. Every deployment teaches the next one. Your job is to make that loop turn faster and teach more each time. Responsibilities Set the research agenda for Cortex: vision-language-action models, world models and planning, learning from interaction on real robots, and generalization across tasks and embodiments. Make the big bets: which directions get people and compute, and which ones we stop. Own the data strategy: the mix of deployment, teleoperation, open-source and synthetic data, and what the fleet collects next. Own the compute strategy, from large-scale training to real-time inference on the robot. Build the evaluation science: benchmarks that predict performance in a customer’s operation, not only on a leaderboard. Build and lead the research organisation in Zurich and Stuttgart: structure, leads, rhythm. Set the hiring bar and make Sereact the place the best people in robot learning want to join. Take research into production with engineering, so results reach the fleet in weeks and hold up in 24/7 operation. Decide with the founders what we publish, open-source or patent, and build our standing at CoRL, RSS, ICRA, NeurIPS and ICML. Be Sereact’s scientific voice with customers, partners, universities and investors, and build academic partnerships. Partner with the CTO, product and operations, so research, engineering and deployment pull in one direction. Not in scope, by design Software platform, hardware and field deployment engineering. They stay with the CTO and operations: the CTO owns how we build and ship, you own what we learn next. A research lab beside the business. Research at Sereact ends on a robot, ideally at a customer. Product roadmap and pricing. What makes this role hard Research and production compete for the same robots, people and compute. You make that trade-off every week, in the open. Cortex is not a blank page. It already runs in customer operations, and our founders are deeply technical. You raise the ceiling of a running system. A result counts when it holds up in a customer’s operation, not when the paper is accepted. Your first 12 months First 90 days: know the fleet, the data and the team; agree the research roadmap with the founders; one evaluation standard everyone uses. By month 6: a research organisation with clear ownership and a release rhythm from experiment to fleet. By month 12: a new generation of Cortex in customer operations with measurable gains, key senior hires made, and work that puts Sereact on the map of robot learning. What you bring You have led research in robot learning or embodied AI (VLA models, imitation or reinforcement learning, world models) and built a team around it. Your work runs on real robots, ideally outside the lab and for long stretches. You know what breaks first. Scientific standing: a strong record at the top venues and a network that great researchers want to join. You have made real calls on research bets, data and compute, and stopped what did not work. You explain science to engineers, customers and investors alike, and you enjoy it. PhD in machine learning, robotics or a related field, or an equivalent track record. Nice to have: large-scale pretraining of foundation models · fleet learning or data engines · industrial manipulation · experience in both academia and industry. Three questions we will ask you Tell us about a model you took from a paper to a robot that ran for weeks without you. What broke first? If you had our deployment data tomorrow, which bet would you make first, and what would you stop? How do you decide what to publish and what to keep? What we offer Robots in live production that learn every day, and the data that comes with them. A seat in the leadership team of a company scaling from Europe into the US, with meaningful equity. Large-scale compute and the freedom to build the research organisation you would want to work in. Teams in Stuttgart, Zurich and Boston; relocation support. How we hire Conversations with both founders, a research deep dive with the team, and a working session on a real problem from our deployments. We move fast. Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

description: About Orakl Oncology Every cancer patient deserves a treatment that works for them. Today, too many never get one in time: fewer than 5% of new cancer drugs make it through clinical trials, and every failure costs patients precious time. Orakl exists to change those odds. We bridge biological and artificial intelligence by building large cohorts of virtual cancer patients, combining real patients' tumors with their medical histories and deep biological data. By integrating patient-derived tumor models, experimental biology and AI, we help pharmaceutical companies predict how cancer drugs will perform in patients, identify promising treatments and make better decisions earlier in drug development. Founded in 2023 by Fanny Jaulin, PhD, Diane-Laure Pagès, PhD, and Gustave Ronteix, PhD, Orakl is a spin-out of Gustave Roussy, one of Europe's leading cancer centres, building on a decade of research. Backed by international investors, we are scaling our technology and partnerships with pharmaceutical companies worldwide. Discover more at orakl-oncology.com The role We are looking for our first Communications, Brand & Events Lead to build Orakl's external presence from the ground up and establish the company as a leading voice in AI-driven cancer drug development. Your job is to make the world understand what we are building, why it matters and why Orakl is uniquely positioned to lead this transformation. You will shape how Orakl is perceived by the pharmaceutical companies we partner with, the scientists we want to attract, the investors backing us and the broader industry. From defining our corporate narrative and building our reputation to securing media coverage and putting Orakl in the right rooms, you will turn our scientific and commercial progress into visibility, credibility and meaningful relationships. You will own our communications, brand and events strategy, working directly with the founders and closely with our scientific, BD and Product Marketing teams. While Product Marketing focuses on our offerings and their commercial value, you will own Orakl's corporate voice, reputation and external presence. You will also lead internal events and support on internal brand alignment. This is a strategic but highly hands-on role. You will set the direction, build the function and execute much of it yourself, with the autonomy to experiment, make decisions and shape how Orakl grows. You will need to combine the speed and creativity of a startup with the standards of the pharmaceutical industry. Our communications must be distinctive and ambitious, but always grounded in scientific rigour, evidence and credibility. What you'll do Communications and brand: building Orakl's voice Communications strategy. Define and execute Orakl's communications strategy across audiences, channels and markets, setting clear priorities that support the company's commercial, scientific, talent and fundraising ambitions. Corporate positioning and narrative. Own Orakl's corporate story, key messages and tone of voice. Build a distinctive narrative around virtual patients and Orakl's role in advancing cancer drug development, ensuring consistency across the company. Brand identity and presence. Own and evolve Orakl's brand identity and visual expression across the website, corporate materials, presentations and digital channels, working with designers and external partners when needed. Content and editorial strategy. Build and manage an editorial calendar that turns Orakl's scientific breakthroughs, company milestones and industry perspectives into compelling content for the right audiences. Founders' voice and thought leadership. Build the public profiles of Orakl's founders through LinkedIn, articles, op-eds, interviews and relevant scientific and industry channels. Identify the topics and conversations where Orakl can bring a distinctive perspective. Press and media relations. Develop relationships with scientific, pharmaceutical, technology and business media. Identify newsworthy stories, pitch proactively and lead communications around funding, partnerships, scientific advances and company milestones. Speaking opportunities. Build and pitch a targeted pipeline of speaking engagements, panels, podcasts and interviews that position Orakl's founders and scientific leaders as recognised voices in the industry. Reputation and scientific credibility. Ensure all external communications are accurate, evidence-based and consistent with Orakl's scientific standards. Help manage sensitive announcements, complex topics and reputational issues in close collaboration with leadership and scientific teams. Events: putting Orakl in the right room Events strategy and prioritization. Build Orakl's annual events strategy and calendar, identifying the conferences, industry gatherings and scientific forums that matter most to the business (e.g. JPM, BIO, AACR, BIO-Europe). Define objectives, budgets and expected outcomes for each. Conference presence and execution. Own Orakl's participation in major industry events, from sponsorships, booths and speaking opportunities to registrations, logistics, travel, vendors and on-site execution. Business development activation. Work closely with BD and the founders to identify priority contacts, secure relevant meetings and build targeted engagement programmes around key events. Ensure opportunities are captured and followed up. Orakl-hosted events. Create and run Orakl's own event formats, from intimate scientific dinners and executive roundtables to webinars and partner gatherings, designed to strengthen relationships and generate meaningful conversations. Event content and experience. Own invitations, event branding, booth design, signage and communications before, during and after events, working with Product Marketing on offering-specific and scientific commercial content. Event performance. Evaluate the impact of Orakl's events against their objectives, including strategic relationships developed, meetings secured, commercial opportunities generated and visibility achieved. Use these insights to refine future investments. Internal communications and culture Internal events. Plan and deliver company off-sites, all-hands gatherings and team celebrations that bring people together and strengthen Orakl's culture. Internal brand alignment. Help teams understand and consistently communicate Orakl's mission, narrative and positioning, ensuring a coherent company voice as the organisation grows. Building the function Processes and partners. Establish the tools, workflows and external partner network needed to deliver high-quality communications and events efficiently, managing agencies, freelancers and budgets. Measurement and priorities. Define how communications and events success is measured, focusing on quality of visibility, audience relevance, reputation, strategic relationships and contribution to company objectives. Cross-functional collaboration. Work closely with founders, BD, scientific teams and Product Marketing to identify the strongest stories, align priorities and ensure communications supports Orakl's broader ambitions. What we're looking for Experience in communications, PR, brand or a related role, ideally within life sciences, biotech, healthtech or B2B technology. Strong strategic communications skills, with experience developing corporate narratives, positioning and communications plans that support business objectives. Exceptional writing and storytelling ability, from short-form social content and executive ghostwriting to press releases, long-form editorial, website copy and event communications. Experience in media relations and thought leadership, with a track record of securing relevant earned media, interviews or speaking opportunities and building executive profiles. Ability to communicate complex science, translating technical and scientific concepts into compelling, accurate stories for pharma decision-makers, investors, scientists and broader audiences. Strong editorial judgment, with the ability to recognize what is genuinely newsworthy, identify compelling angles and choose the right audience, channel and moment. Experience in events and conference management, from strategic planning and budgeting to hands-on execution, ideally with an understanding of how events can support commercial relationships. A strong eye for brand and design, with the ability to maintain high creative standards across digital and physical touchpoints. Hands-on and entrepreneurial mindset, equally comfortable setting a strategy, writing a LinkedIn post, pitching a journalist or running an event on-site. Autonomy, creativity and pragmatism, with the confidence to work directly with founders, manage multiple priorities and make things happen in a fast-moving startup. Fluent in English, French is a plus. Work on-site with occasional remote work. You don't need to come from a traditional life sciences communications background. We value people who combine strong storytelling instincts, intellectual curiosity, sound judgment and the ability to make complex ideas accessible without compromising their accuracy. What Orakl offers Build something from the ground up. Become Orakl's first Communications, Brand & Events Lead, with the opportunity to define the function, shape its priorities and grow a team as the company scales. Shape the voice of an emerging category. Help establish Orakl as a recognised leader in virtual cancer patients and AI-driven drug development. Work at the frontier of AI and cancer research. Bring breakthrough scientific advances to the audiences and organisations that can turn them into real-world impact. Real ownership and direct access to leadership. Time to recharge. 25 days of paid holiday, plus approximately 9 additional rest days (RTT) per year. Hybrid working. 1–2 days per week occasional work from home. description:
Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale — unleashing the potential of businesses and people. The Elastic Search AI Platform, used by more than 50% of the Fortune 500, brings together the precision of search and the intelligence of AI to enable everyone to accelerate the results that matter. By taking advantage of all structured and unstructured data — securing and protecting private information more effectively — Elastic’s complete, cloud-based solutions for search, security, and observability help organizations deliver on the promise of AI.

What is The Role

Elastic Security is one of the fastest-growing parts of our business, and our customers (including government and public sector organisations) rely on our Security Solution to modernise their SOC, threat detection, and response capabilities.

You will lead the hands-on delivery of Elastic Security projects (new implementations, migrations, and use-case expansions) from discovery through architecture design and build. Along the way, you'll develop trusted relationships with senior stakeholders and work closely with our Services, Engineering and Sales teams.

Elastic is a remote-first company, but many of the projects you'll deliver might require onsite availability, making the role hybrid in practice, varying by project, with travel of up to 60%.
Some of these engagements, given the organisations involved, also require national security screening or clearance; eligibility to obtain one in your country of employment is a strong advantage, and Elastic will sponsor the process where required.

What You Will Be Doing

Assess and Design

  • Analyse customer goals, pain points, existing architecture, and threat landscape, translating them into technical requirements
  • Design Elastic Security solution architectures (SIEM, endpoint, cloud security) that integrate with the customer's wider security ecosystem
  • Advise on the customer's security strategy and own the Elastic side of it, aligning recommendations through regular sessions with senior and key stakeholders

Implement and Deliver

  • Lead hands-on delivery of Elastic Security projects end-to-end, including greenfield deployments and migrations from legacy SIEM/EDR platforms in mission-critical environments
  • Deploy and secure the Elastic platform: cluster architecture, RBAC and role mapping, single sign-on, private connectivity (private links, VPC peering), and hardening for enterprise and government environments
  • Architect and build large-scale data ingestion with Elastic Agent, Beats, and Logstash, normalising data to ECS and integrating sources such as Kafka, Azure Event Hub, and AWS S3
  • Develop security content aligned to the customer's threat landscape: detection rules, dashboards, and alerting workflows
  • Drive security migrations from competing platforms, applying deep knowledge of Elastic's capabilities to translate each use case into its best form, whether through feature parity mapping or full redesign
  • Establish detection-as-code practices for customers managing detections programmatically: developing, testing, versioning, and deploying detection content with Python, Git, and CI/CD pipelines
  • Apply and enable Elastic's Agentic AI capabilities (AI Assistant, Attack Discovery, agent-driven workflows) to accelerate customers' detection and response

Grow and Collaborate

  • Identify and deliver new security use cases as customers mature their cyber defence journey with Elastic
  • Deliver engagements on time and within the agreed Statement of Work (SOW) scope, surfacing opportunities for follow-on work
  • Communicate confidently with stakeholders from SOC engineers up to CISO / C-suite level
  • Partner with Elastic Sales and pre-sales to assess technical risks and shape opportunities
  • Feed field insight back to Elastic Engineering, Product Management, and Support to drive feature enhancements
  • Mentor and share knowledge with fellow Elastic consultants across a highly distributed team
  • Lead or assist with demos and proof-of-concepts that showcase the value of the Elastic Stack, and deliver enablement sessions and hands-on workshops that make customer teams self-sufficient

What You Bring Along

  • Minimum of 5 years' experience as a Consulting Architect, Senior Consultant, or in a senior IT technical leadership role, delivering and executing professional services engagements, ideally in the security domain
  • Solid experience deploying Elastic Security or comparable SIEM platforms (e.g., Splunk, MS Sentinel, QRadar, ArcSight) and/or EDR platforms (e.g., CrowdStrike, MS Defender), or at least 2 years as a Security Analyst / Detection Engineer in a threat detection and response role
  • An architect's view of the security ecosystem across varied customer environments: SOAR, vulnerability management, penetration testing, ticketing, and security policies, and how they connect in a SOC
  • Scripting skills, ideally in Python, and exposure to modern delivery practices such as Infrastructure-as-Code and CI/CD are strongly preferred
  • Hands-on experience with Linux and Windows operating systems, and on-prem and/or public cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP)
  • Strong customer advocacy, relationship-building, and communication skills, with the ability to pivot easily between delivery and strategic engagements
  • Eligibility to obtain national security clearance in your country of employment (screening sponsored by Elastic where required)
  • Willingness to travel and work onsite with customers (up to 60% of the time), combined with comfort working remotely in a highly distributed team
  • Strong proficiency in both English (our company-wide operating language) and the local market language.

Bonus Points

  • Experience with advanced Elasticsearch operations: cluster architecture, shard management, data ingestion, and data tiering at scale
  • Experience with detection-as-code: authoring, testing, and versioning detection content managed in Git
  • Experience automating deployments and lifecycle management with Python, Terraform, and CI/CD tooling (e.g., GitLab pipelines)
  • Experience deploying and operating containerised workloads on Kubernetes, cloud-managed or self-hosted (EKS, AKS, GKE, OpenShift)
  • Experience with Agentic AI and LLM-based security workflows: AI assistants, automated triage, and agent-driven investigation
  • Experience as a Tier-2/Tier-3 SOC Analyst, Threat Hunter, or DevSecOps Engineer
  • Experience in large distributed environments or MSSPs, from architecture through deployment
  • Experience delivering enablement sessions, technical workshops, or product training to technical audiences
  • Elastic Certified Engineer certification, or security certifications such as GIAC or CISSP

Notre équipe Data Governance recherche un·e Data Governance Project Manager basé·e à Lille 

Chez Decathlon, nous croyons au pouvoir du sport pour unir et inspirer. 

Notre mission : rendre le sport accessible au plus grand nombre, partout dans le monde. Pour y parvenir, la data est au cœur de notre stratégie, elle guide chaque décision, de la conception du produit à l'expérience client Notre défi ? La rendre gouvernée, sûre et accessible à tous. 

Tu rejoindras le Data Governance Center of Excellence pour transformer nos politiques théoriques en réalités opérationnelles. Ta mission est double : Améliorer les dispositifs de contrôles de la données et garantir la conformité de nos actifs via un framework d’audit robuste. 

TA MISSION : ORGANISER LA STRATEGIE D'AUDIT ET DE CONTRÔLE DE NOS STANDARDS DE GOUVERNANCE

1. Stratégie d’Audit & Compliance

Ton rôle est de mesurer la conformité de l'organisation à nos standards de gouvernance sur l’intégralité de notre scope. 

  • Framework de Contrôle vs Audit : Définir la ligne de démarcation entre le contrôle continu (opérationnel/automatique) et l'audit périodique (stratégique/qualitatif).
  • Industrialisation : Identifier les contrôles éligibles à l’automatisation (ex: intégrité référentielle, fraîcheur via les Data Contracts) et piloter leur mise en œuvre avec les équipes Data Engineering.
  • Audit des "Invisibles" : Concevoir les protocoles(y compris plan d’audit, cartographie des risques et déclenchement de mission ad hoc) d'audit pour les critères non-automatisables (pertinence du dictionnaire de données, qualité des descriptions, respect des processus de classification Privacy), identifier les root cause, les risques et les responsabilités.
  • Gestion des non conformités : Définir la stratégie de suivi des écarts. Tu ne te contentes pas de pointer les problèmes, tu bâtis le framework qui aide les équipes à corriger le tir (scoring, plans d'actions, escalade).

2. Structuration

Tu jouera pleinement ton rôle dans la définition et dans l’amélioration continue de l’operating modèle des audits et des contrôles

  • Mandat : Faire valider le niveau de sponsor et de validation du mandat général et/ou des fiches de mission pour assurer le bon niveau d’engagement des audités. Les décisions devront s’articuler autour du cadre général d’Audit interne de Decathlon
  • Reporting : Communiquer les résultats des travaux et assurer le suivi de la mise en oeuvre des recommandations et, le cas échéant, du processus d’escalade
  • Interactions : Formaliser et faire vivre les rituels et procédures permettant d’optimiser les synergies entre les travaux d’audit et de contrôle et ceux des autres équipes de la gouvernance fédérée (Expertise & projets de CoE en particulier)

CE QUE TU APPORTES

  • Expertise en Gouvernance & Data Architecture : Tu maîtrises les frameworks de référence (DAMA/DMBOK), tu comprends les enjeux des architectures modernes (architecture médaillon, Data Contracts, Data Product) et les formats de structuration de données (YAML/JSON)
  • Culture de l'Audit & de la Conformité : Tu as une solide expérience dans la définition de standards, de normes et de protocoles d'audit. Tu sais distinguer un contrôle opérationnel d'un audit de gouvernance et tu es capable de transformer un constat d'écart en un plan de remédiation pragmatique (KRI/KPI)
  • Leadership d'Influence & Change : Tu es à l’aise dans l'animation de communautés (Data Stewards, Producers). Tu sais vulgariser des sujets complexes, lever les points de friction entre technique et business, et porter une vision de "Gouvernance by design"

description: Data Scientist - Credit Risk Modelling Hybrid in London or remote in the UK We’re looking for a Data Scientist to join our Credit Risk Modelling team. You'll work on the credit models that sit at the core of iwoca's lending business – the models that decide who we lend to, on what terms, and how far the product can grow. The company Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are. That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed. We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive. The team The Credit Risk Modelling team owns credit risk and customer lifetime value (CLtV) modelling for iwoca's UK and German lending. That covers the probabilistic machine learning models behind every credit decision, plus the CLtV models that shape pricing and portfolio strategy. The team is around twelve data scientists, who combined create models to efficiently drive fully automated and human-in-the-loop decision making. This forms the core analytical team that interface with and support smaller analytic functions in other parts of the business. The role You'll run credit and CLtV modelling projects alongside the rest of the team. The work spans keeping production models healthy, incremental development, and research that reshapes how the models work. AI has lowered the cost of prototyping enough that ideas which used to sit below the priority line are now viable, so the R&D share of the role is growing. Live examples of the work: Causal estimation of offer terms. Modelling how amount, duration, and price shape customer outcomes. Unifying auto and manual models. The two families were built without forced technical alignment. Finding a principled way to unify them on a common cost function is open work. IFRS accounting model. A multi-stage credit model where information propagates back from later-stage recovery predictions to sharpen upfront loss estimates. Generalising credit and CLtV. Whether a more general framing could replace both separate models is an open research question. The requirements Essential: Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience. Statistical foundations. You have a background in probability and statistics from a quantitative field. You reason about uncertainty and calibration as first-order concerns. Research mindset. You're actively exploring new ways to add value. R&D time is when you expect to find the next step change. Judgement. You critically evaluate model output – yours, a colleague's, or an LLM's – and can explain why a choice is right. You defend your reasoning under challenge, and challenge others' when the evidence points elsewhere. Analytical ownership. You take ambiguous problems end to end, from framing to a landed decision. You like to move fast, iterate, and update on new evidence rather than chase perfection. AI fluency. You use AI as a primary tool. You prototype with it, automate with it, and take on R&D that would not otherwise be viable. You use judgement on where it helps and where it doesn't. Bonus: Domain experience. You have worked in credit risk, lending, or customer lifetime value modelling. Production ML. You have built and shipped supervised ML models end to end – exploration, training, deployment, monitoring. Non-linear methods. You can think in terms of the cost function and inductive biases of your models Bayesian methods. You have used hierarchical models, MCMC, or Bayesian updating in real work. Time series modelling. You have modelled temporal data where autocorrelation, drift, or seasonality mattered. Python. The stack the team uses. The salary We expect to pay from £60,000 – £90,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews. The culture At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective. We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them. The offices We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work: Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks. Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions. The benefits Flexible working hours. Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership. A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents. 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave. A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years. Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support. 3% Pension contributions on total earnings. An employee equity incentive scheme. Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money. Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme. Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield. And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer: A learning and development budget for everyone. Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers. Access to learning platforms like Treehouse. About Ping Identity: 

At Ping Identity, we believe in making digital experiences both secure and seamless for all users, without compromise. We call this digital freedom. And it's not just something we provide our customers. It's something that inspires our company. People don't come here to join a culture that's built on digital freedom. They come to cultivate it. 

Our intelligent, cloud identity platform lets people shop, work, bank, and interact wherever and however they want. Without friction. Without fear. 

While protecting digital identities is at the core of our technology, protecting individual identities is at the core of our culture. We champion every identity. One of our core values, Respect Individuality, reminds us to celebrate differences so you are empowered to bring your authentic self to work. 

We're headquartered in Denver, Colorado and we have offices and employees around the globe. We serve the largest, most demanding enterprises worldwide, including more than half of the Fortune 100. At Ping Identity, we're changing the way people and businesses think about cybersecurity, digital experiences, and identity and access management. 

The Sales Director will have full Middle East territory responsibility and will be tasked with influencing and developing an energized, competitive, high impact sales team that is characterized by its ability to create differentiated value for our customer base.

We’re looking for a seasoned leader from within the SaaS enterprise marketplace, with proven software solution selling combined with success in a fast growth business. This leader will be a model to drive the team in building extraordinary customer relationships and experiences, leveraging a strong teamwork approach, and cross matrix collaboration across all Ping functions. This role will demonstrate a depth of understanding when working alongside a partner community and posess a well-established customer and partner network in the Middle East region. 

In order to acquire, develop and retain customer relationships and create a winning Ping business, this leader will be able to create and maintain a high-performance culture, that is grounded in data, transparency, accountability, and agility. The ideal candidate’s mindset should be customer-focused, people-oriented, open, passionate, and authentic. 

 

Responsibilities:

  • Creates, implements, measures and reviews a strategic or operational plan that drives achievement of business goals aligned to overall Ping strategy
  • Uses mechanisms such as territory planning, account plans, opportunity inspection, pipeline management, account reviews, forecast calls, etc.
  • Advises and coaches the sales team around how to position and articulate Ping Identity’s value proposition at enterprise customers, thus increasing the average deal size
  • Identifies and pursues opportunities to expand business activities within areas of responsibility
  • Leverages GSIs & other partners to help source, develop and progress business
  • Plans and controls the expense associated with the area of responsibility even if not responsible for overall cost center
  • Establishes working relationships with external parties which supports the achievement of business goals
  • Is conversant with Ping Identity’s systems and procedures and ensures effective use of and conformance to standard business practices and tools (i.e. SFDC – SalesForce.com)
  • Communicates Ping Identity’s vision and aligns team and personal goals to achieve business results
  • Provides direction and guidance, mentoring and development of the field team
  • Lives teamwork and promotes cross-functional collaboration
  • Recruits, builds and develops the team to deliver business results; Identifies, develops and promotes high potential employees
  • Recommends and/or approves people-related decisions – hiring, promotions, merit increases, rewards & recognition, training initiatives, etc.
  • Drives performance review and development planning process with annual and quarterly review meetings
  • Has established multi-vertical C level contacts in large enterprise customers
  • Has an established partner/SI network and is used to working with partners on projects
  • Builds relationships with customers (internal or external) as necessary providing customer escalation management as necessary for problem resolution
  • Provides support for customer relationship management as necessary and drives initiatives which result in improvement in customer satisfaction
  • Drives initiatives which result in improvement in customer satisfaction

 

Required Skills & Qualifications:

  • Proven experience of successfully leading sales teams focused on the Middle East territory
  • Expertise in enterprise software, SaaS, managed services and strategic account management
  • Results-oriented with multiple years meeting or exceeding quota
  • Flexibility to travel to the Middle East region 
  • Transitioned a team through on-prem to SaaS solutions
  • Adept working in a fast-growing global organization
  • Good interpersonal skills to align and foster positive working relationships across the organization

 

Life at Ping:

We believe in and facilitate a flexible, collaborative work environment. We’re growing quickly, but remain true to the innovative, can-do startup values that got us here. Most importantly, we keep hiring talented, smart, fun, and genuinely nice people because that’s who we want to succeed with every day. 

Here are just a few of the things that make Ping special:

  • A company culture that empowers you to do your best work.
  • Employee Resource Groups that create a sense of belonging for everyone.
  • Regular company and team bonding events.
  • Competitive benefits and perks.
  • Global volunteering and community initiatives

Our Benefits: 

  • Generous PTO & Holiday Schedule 
  • Parental Leave
  • Progressive Healthcare Options
  • Retirement Programs
  • Opportunity for Education Reimbursement 
  • Commuter Offset (Specific locations) 

Ping is the collective sum of all our individual experiences, backgrounds and influences and we pride ourselves in growing and learning together. We are committed to building an inclusive and diverse environment where everyone’s individuality is respected and everyone has an Identity. In recruiting for new colleagues, we welcome the unique contributions you can bring and encourage you to be your best self.

We are an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer.  All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex including sexual orientation and gender identity, national origin, disability, protected Veteran Status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Forecast Accuracy: Maintain a high level of "Sales Hygiene" within CRM, delivering predictable weekly and monthly forecasts aligned with SAP’s rigorous reporting standards.

Onapsis protects the business applications that run the global economy. The Onapsis Platform delivers vulnerability management, change assurance, and continuous compliance for business applications from leading vendors such as SAP, Oracle, and others. The Onapsis Platform is powered by the Onapsis Research Labs, the team responsible for the discovery and mitigation of more than 1,000 zero-day vulnerabilities in business applications.

Onapsis is headquartered in Boston, MA, with offices in Dallas, TX, Heidelberg, Germany, Bucharest, Romania, and Buenos Aires, Argentina, and proudly serves hundreds of the world’s leading brands, including close to 30% of the Forbes Global 100, six of the top 10 automotive companies, five of the top 10 chemical companies, four of the top 10 technology companies, and three of the top 10 oil and gas companies.

Die het grotere plaatje ziet, maar net zo makkelijk de diepte ingaat om een financieel vraagstuk op te lossen. Wat ga je doen? Je voelt je comfortabel op beide niveaus. Wie zoeken we? We zoeken een Financial Director die financiële expertise combineert met ondernemerschap, leiderschap en een sterk gevoel voor de business. Ervaring in een hardware-, productie-, energie-, logistieke of andere werkkapitaalintensieve omgeving is een groot voordeel. Het vermogen om een financiële functie en team op te bouwen, zonder zelf de aansluiting met de dagelijkse praktijk te verliezen. Affiniteit met technologie, automatisering en AI. description:
As a Forward Deployed Engineer at Auterion, you will play a pivotal role in the successful development, integration and deployment of Auterion-powered drone systems. 

In this role, you will collaborate closely with the production, hardware engineering, and firmware/software teams, as well as operations, ensuring that every platform transitions smoothly from an airframe concept into a fully validated flying robot ready for deployment. You will serve as the primary technical interface for partners, work closely with them to understand their technical requirements, configure and adapt existing solutions, contribute to core software development, and ensure successful implementation. 

This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys combining hands-on technical work with customer collaboration and system-level problem solving, bridging the gap between hardware, firmware, and real-world flight performance. 

Responsibilities and Duties

  • Operate in a highly hands-on environment with evolving system requirements, rapidly iterating across hardware and software integration challenges.
  • Manage software releases and perform firmware flashing and configuration using PX4 or adjacent autopilot ecosystems, including sensor calibration, ESC tuning, and system bring-up.
  • Provide deep avionics and airframe expertise, including autopilot tuning, sensor and payload integration, power systems and airworthiness considerations.
  • Work independently to troubleshoot integration and flight-readiness issues while collaborating cross-functionally with hardware engineering, firmware/software teams, operations, and QC engineering to escalate complex challenges when required.
  • Act as the primary technical authority in customer engagements, translating mission requirements into concrete system architectures and demonstrable solutions built on AuterionOS and Skynode.
  • Participate in flight testing activities to validate platform stability, safety, and mission performance, resolving technical issues often directly in the field during customer trials and demonstrations.
  • Contribute to technical documentation and continuous improvement of engineering processes.
  • Feed customer and market requirements back into product and engineering teams to influence the roadmap of the Auterion stack.

Qualifications and Skills

  • Degree in Software, Electrical, Mechanical, Aerospace or Robotics Engineering, or a related field
  • Working proficiency in C/C++ and Python: you can read, debug and patch existing code and write small tools and scripts
  • Comfortable in Linux environments, including the command line, logs, Docker and basic networking (IP, TCP/UDP)
  • Hands-on hardware-software integration: system bring-up, wiring and connectors, and embedded interfaces (UART, CAN, I2C, SPI) at a practical level
  • Structured troubleshooting: you can isolate whether a problem is software, hardware, configuration or RF, often under time pressure in the field
  • Strong communicator: you can explain technical issues clearly to customers and operators, and report findings back to engineering in a way they can act on
  • Willing to travel and work on-site with customers, including at test ranges and in field environments
  • EU citizenship (required for security clearance and customer requirements)

Nice-to-have

  • Experience with PX4 or ArduPilot, MAVLink, QGroundControl or mission planning tools
  • UAV flight testing and validation in operational environments
  • Experience with datalinks and radio systems
  • Previous customer-facing or field engineering role, especially with defense or government customers
  • German language skills

Benefits

  • Flexible working hours
  • Stock Options
  • Generous holiday allowance
  • Pension plan 
  • Extended social security package 
  • Enhanced maternity & paternity leave

About Auterion

We are building the leading software platform for AI-powered autonomous systems for enterprise and government customers. Our team is supporting the most important missions and solving the most challenging problems.

At Auterion, we bring together the sharpest minds who love to solve the hardest problems. Join a vibrant team built on innovation, openness, and excellence, where you’ll be empowered to develop ideas, collaborate across all levels, and make an impact that matters.

description: ENVIRONNEMENT DU POSTE : École du ministère en charge de l'industrie, IMT Mines Albi est une école de l’Institut Mines- Télécom, 1er groupe d’écoles d’ingénieurs et de management de France. À l'avant-garde des enjeux industriels et académiques sur la scène internationale, elle agit comme un moteur scientifique et économique territorial en combinant ses 4 missions - former des ingénieurs en intégrant la dynamique du développement durable, faire de la recherche scientifique, contribuer au développement économique et diffuser la culture des sciences, des techniques et de l'innovation - en un cercle vertueux et porteur d'innovation. Son positionnement en matière de formation et de recherche la place IMT Mines Albi comme école de référence sur trois des quatre thématiques de l’IMT, à savoir l’industrie du futur responsable, l’énergie, économie circulaire et société ainsi que l’ingénierie, santé et bien-être. IMT Mines Albi s‘est dotée en 2023 et pour une période quinquennale, d’un plan stratégique décliné en 7 grandes actions, répondant ainsi aux orientations stratégiques du groupe IMT à laquelle elle appartient. IMT Mines Albi, au travers du Centre Génie Industriel (CGI), développe des recherches à la frontière entre l’intelligence artificielle et le génie industriel, en collaboration avec des partenaires publics et industriels nationaux et internationaux. Le Centre Génie Industriel (CGI) (https://cgi.imt-mines-albi.fr/) compte environ 70 personnes dont 25 doctorants. Le centre s’intéresse à l’accompagnement de la transition des écosystèmes en permettant de prendre des décisions responsables et durables, dans des environnements instables ou perturbés. Ceci est mis en pratique par la représentation, la modélisation et l’analyse des données de ces organisations afin de formaliser de la connaissance conduisant à la prise de décision dans des contextes hétérogènes, collaboratifs, incertains et/ou perturbés. Le CGI est structuré selon des axes de recherche appliquée et des programmes scientifiques. Les axes de recherche appliquée sont : Axe FLOWS : Flexible Logistics and Operations for sustainable WorldS dans lequel ce poste est rattaché. Axe DiSCS : Digital Systems for Crisis management and Security ; Axe TRACE : Territorial Resilience, Agility, and Circular Economy ; Axe WHOPS : Well-being and Health through Organizational Processes and Services. Les deux programmes scientifiques au cœur de ces axes de recherche sont : HOPOPOP : Hybridization for Operations & Planning, Organizations & Performance, Optimization & Problem-solving ; AIME-DM : Automated Information Modeling and Extraction for Decision-Makers. DESCRIPTION DU POSTE : Dans le contexte de l’Education 4.0, les différents acteurs d’un établissement de formation universitaire (étudiants, personnels, intervenants extérieurs, etc.) ont des contraintes et des objectifs différents ce qui rend complexe la coordination et le pilotage de tels établissements (organisation et planification des enseignements, gestion des espaces collectifs, organisation des sessions d’examens…). En complément, ces établissements doivent s’adapter tant sur la gestion de leurs sites (meilleure adéquation à de nouvelles formes pédagogiques) que sur les flux de personnes les utilisant pour une meilleure répartition des charges et une interopérabilité de tous les outils à disposition (par exemple, un gestionnaire d’emploi du temps). Dans ce cadre, le jumeau numérique organisationnel représente le système qui permet une simulation et une aide à la prise de décision par des échanges bidirectionnels entre l’organisation physique (personnes et systèmes dont les bâtiments) et sa réplique virtuelle dans un objectif de pilotage global des flux. Le projet DIGIFAC’Santé s’inscrit dans ce contexte. Il porte sur la conception et le développement d'un jumeau numérique des sites d’une université, de la gestion des flux étudiants et personnels et de l’évolution pédagogique de ses formations. Un jumeau numérique ne peut remplir son rôle qu'à la condition de représenter fidèlement les informations essentielles à la prise de décision, elles-mêmes issues de données collectées dans les différents services de l’Université et des applications logicielles actuelles. Or, ces applications présentent des niveaux d’hétérogénéité différents selon leurs fonctionnalités. La nature des opérations réalisées (emploi du temps, gestion des salles et du matériel, etc.) impose des contraintes fortes sur la disponibilité de ces données : leur collecte automatique et en temps réel n'est pas toujours techniquement envisageable, ce qui constitue un défi central pour l'alimentation du jumeau numérique. L’étude à mener dans le cadre de ce projet vise à : Modéliser le besoin informationnel. Il s'agit de concevoir un méta-modèle capable de représenter, de façon générique et formelle, les informations strictement nécessaires à l’alimentation du jumeau numérique universitaire. Ce méta-modèle doit permettre de cadrer la remontée d'information en définissant le juste besoin, c'est-à-dire en distinguant ce qui relève de l'information décisionnelle de ce qui constitue un artefact de collecte sans valeur ajoutée pour le pilotage. Alimenter les modèles. Une fois le méta-modèle du besoin informationnel établi, la question de son instanciation à partir de données réelles des applications existantes se pose. Comment alimenter ces modèles à partir de données hétérogènes, partielles, et produites selon des rythmes et des modalités de collecte variables ? Ceci articule des enjeux d'intégration, de qualité et de cohérence de la donnée au regard des exigences du jumeau numérique. Gérer l'absence de certaines données. Dans un contexte où certaines opérations ne permettent pas une collecte automatique et en temps réel, en raison de la nature même des processus mis en place (par exemple, construction de l’emploi du temps, suivi des cohortes d’étudiants), comment maintenir la cohérence et la complétude de la représentation portée par le jumeau numérique ? Ce lot interroge la capacité du système à pallier les lacunes de la remontée de données par des mécanismes d'inférence ou de déduction, permettant de reconstituer un état vraisemblable du système à partir d'informations partielles. Proposer des aides au dimensionnement et au pilotage des sites universitaires. Il s’agit ici d’utiliser le jumeau numérique dans toutes ses fonctionnalités afin entres autres de s’assurer que les évolutions bâtimentaires envisagées permettent d’accueillir l’ensemble des flux actuel et projeté pour cet établissement, de permettre d’optimiser les flux entre les différents sites et de valider les choix d’évolution des pratiques pédagogiques et leur adéquation vis à vis des capacités disponibles (salles et équipements spécifiques, surfaces, personnels,etc.). Compétences, connaissances et expériences souhaitables : Modélisation des processus / d’organisation Analyse systémique Analyse de données Ingénierie dirigée par les modèles Aide à la décision Simulation à évènements discrets et jumeau numérique Fouille de processus (process mining), Des connaissances en algorithmique, UML, Web sémantique seront très appréciées Capacités et aptitudes : Anglais écrit et parlé (Niveau B2 minimum exigé) ; cf. référentiel européen ; ex. : 785/990 minimum au TOEIC), attesté par une certification reconnue (TOEFL, TOEIC, IELTS). La maîtrise du français (C1 minimum) est exigée afin de faciliter les échanges avec les experts et les acteurs. Capacité à travailler dans une équipe de recherche, autonomie, esprit d’initiative, organisation, curiosité intellectuelle… Motivation pour contribuer à une application universitaire PROFIL RECHERCHE : Ingénieur.e recherche ou post-doctorant, en génie industriel et/ou supply chain management et/ou Génie Logiciel ou Master ou équivalent (niveau Bac+5). AU-DELÀ DE L’ENVIRONNEMENT PROFESSIONNEL, POURQUOI NOUS REJOINDRE ? : cadre de travail agréable dans un campus de 22 ha 49 jours de congés par an restauration administrative sur place aide à la mobilité durable pour le transport domicile-travail action sociale (protection sociale complémentaire et aide aux familles) INFORMATIONS COMPLÉMENTAIRES : Le poste est basé à IMT Mines Albi, Centre Génie Industriel, Albi (France). Des déplacements sont à prévoir sur le site du partenaire du projet à Toulouse (Haute Garonne), France. Nature et durée du contrat : CDD 12 mois À usage interne : Catégorie du poste et métier de référence : Catégorie II, Métier R – Ingénieur de recherche Métier(s) de référence des agents pouvant postuler : Toutes catégories Localisation du poste : IMT Mines Albi, Campus Jarlard, Route de Teillet 81013 ALBI CT Cedex 09 Date limite de candidature : 22/11/2026 Date de prise de fonction souhaitée : 01/01/2027 La rémunération est fixée selon le profil du candidat (métier, âge, filière d'emploi, durée de garantie salariale), en fonction des règles définies par le cadre de gestion de l'Institut Mines Télécom Les postes offerts au recrutement sont ouverts à toutes et tous avec, sur demande, des aménagements pour les candidates et candidats en situation de handicap Emploi ouvert aux titulaires de catégorie A de la fonction publique et/ou aux personnes contractuelles Contacts : o Sur le contenu du poste : Didier Gourc (o Sur les aspects administratifs/RH: Laura OLIVIER, Gestionnaire RH ( Find Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

description: Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecrafts for humanity. The Avionics, Guidance, Navigation and Control (GNC), and Flight Software (FSW) functions are central to the safe and reliable operation of the vehicle. Together, they provide the electronic systems, control capabilities and software that guide Nyx through its mission - from launch and on-orbit operations to docking, re-entry and recovery. We are looking for a motivated and experienced Project Manager — Avionics, GNC & Flight Software to coordinate the development and delivery of these critical domains within the Nyx program. Your Mission As Project Manager for Avionics, GNC and Flight Software, you will be responsible for coordinating the execution of these work packages and ensuring that their development remains aligned with the overall Nyx program objectives. You will work closely with Avionics, GNC and FSW technical leads, systems engineering, propulsion, mission operations, verification and integration teams. Your role will be to create transparency on scope, schedule, interfaces, risks and decisions, while supporting the teams in delivering robust and well-verified capabilities for the vehicle. This is a highly cross-functional role for someone who enjoys working at the interface between technical teams, program management and mission execution. Key Responsibilities Own and coordinate the project planning for the Avionics, GNC and FSW work packages within the Nyx program. Translate program objectives and major milestones into clear plans, priorities and deliverables for the relevant teams. Coordinate closely with the Avionics, GNC and FSW technical leads to monitor progress, identify blockers and support timely decisions. Coordinate inputs to design reviews, development reviews, qualification activities and other program milestones. Track the preparation and closure of requirements, verification activities, test results, documentation and technical actions. Identify schedule and delivery risks early, define mitigation actions with the relevant owners and escalate unresolved issues when required. Support the management of changes to scope, requirements, interfaces and priorities, ensuring that their impacts are understood. Prepare clear progress updates, decision material and status reports for program and project reviews. Facilitate regular coordination meetings and ensure that actions, decisions and commitments are recorded and followed through. Contribute to resource and capacity planning for the GNC and FSW activities. Support coordination with external partners, suppliers and customers when relevant to the project scope. Contribute to the continuous improvement of project-management processes, planning practices and reporting routines within the Nyx program. Experience coordinating complex technical work packages involving multiple teams and interfaces. Practical experience managing plans, milestones, dependencies, risks, actions and technical deliverables. The ability to understand technical topics sufficiently to ask the right questions, identify impacts and support informed decisions. Experience working across requirements, design, implementation, integration, testing and verification activities. Strong organizational and communication skills, with the ability to bring structure and transparency to complex projects. A proactive approach to identifying risks, raising issues early and driving actions to closure. The ability to work effectively with technical experts while maintaining focus on program objectives and delivery commitments. Experience with project-management, planning, requirements-management or engineering tools. A degree or equivalent experience in aerospace engineering, software engineering, systems engineering, project management or a related field. Professional fluency in English. You can move between detailed technical discussions and program-level decision-making without losing sight of the overall objective. You bring structure without creating unnecessary bureaucracy. You are proactive in identifying dependencies and risks, clear in your communication and persistent in following actions through to closure. You know how to challenge constructively, support technical teams and escalate decisions when the program needs clarity. You are motivated by the opportunity to contribute to a complex space vehicle and understand that reliable GNC and flight software are built through close collaboration, disciplined engineering and continuous verification. Why you should join us! description: About Us QuantWare is building the world’s most powerful quantum processors to solve humanity's greatest challenges. As our Quantum Hardware Assembly Technician at QuantWare, you are the hands that turn a quantum chip into a working, measurable product. You package our chips into their housing and onto a PCB, and you will assemble and mount the new devices into their cryo fridge in the test facility. Your precision, discipline and reliability directly keep our production and measurement pipelines moving, and ensure our quantum hardware meets the highest quality standards. This is a hands-on execution role. You carry out chip assembly and fridge loading according to technical drawings and documented work instructions (SOPs), to a consistent quality standard and pace, and you record your work in our production systems. You report to the Production Manager, who holds formal line-management responsibility (1:1s, performance reviews, absence and leave). You take your daily and weekly priorities from the Assembly Tech Lead, who sets the assembly schedule and is the technical authority on the floor; fridge loading is planned in close coordination with the measurement team. What you'll be doing Core Responsibilities Assemble quantum chips into their packaging, working from technical drawings and work instructions to place and mount the chip in its housing and mount the chip in its housing with the PCB. Make the electrical connections, wirebonding (manual and automatic) will be a significant part of the daily activities, as well as manual soldering. Measure and test your work, performing the defined electrical and mechanical checks and recording the results, so issues are caught before a device moves on. Finish and close the package, including sealing, inspection, laser engraving and preparing for transportation to the measurement location. Load our cryogenic fridges with new chips to be measured, mounting packaged samples and QPUs, making the wiring, thermal and mechanical connections, and closing up the system with magnetic shields. Safeguard quality, handling fragile, high-value parts with care and following handling and ESD procedures, because a single scratch, particle or ESD event can ruin a chip. Supporting Responsibilities Flag deviations early, stopping and raising it with the Assembly Tech Lead when something does not match the instruction or does not look right, rather than improvising a fix. Help improve how we work, giving practical feedback on work instructions, fixtures and tools while our processes are still maturing. Keep a safe, clean and organised workplace, applying 5S and HSE rules every day and making sure your bench, tooling and consumables are ready. Your Profile MBO-level technical education (level 3 or 4) or equivalent, for example in mechatronics, mechanical engineering, electronics, fine-mechanical or precision engineering, or lab or instrument technology. 4+ years of hands-on experience assembling mechanical, electrical or mechatronic systems; relevant internships count. Able to read work instructions with photos and technical drawings, and comfortable with basic digital tools and production systems. Good with your hands at two scales: precision in assembly, handling of fine devices and connectors, and mechanical assembly such as bolting, cabling and fitting larger parts together. Precise and patient, with a genuine liking for detailed hands-on work done well, every time, and a practical approach to solving problems. Comfortable with structured, repeatable work, and disciplined about following instructions step by step and recording what you did. Comfortable in an environment that is still being built, where not every process is finished yet and priorities can shift. A team player in a young, driven team who communicates openly and speaks up when something isn't right. Good command of technical English. Bonus if you also bring: Experience with wirebonding, die attach or other chip-packaging / microelectronics assembly. Experience with measurements, diagnostics or troubleshooting. Experience in a lab, ESD-controlled or 5S production environment. Experience assembling, servicing or setting up complex equipment, instruments or machines. Familiarity with cryogenics or vacuum systems. Don't tick every box? Apply anyway! Research shows women often self-select out if they don't meet every requirement. Here's our take: nobody ticks every box. This is a description of our ideal candidate, not a filter. If most resonates and you're keen to learn the gaps, apply. We hire for trajectory, not perfection. What We Offer: At QuantWare, you’ll be part of a high-performing team of world-class experts in an ambitious, fast-moving environment. From day one, you’ll have the trust, tools, and support to do your best work. Flexibility built on trust - We focus on outcomes. You will own the systems, agents, workflows, and feedback loops that make support better, faster, and more scalable over time. This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who has already operated close to support strategy, technical escalation, user experience, and automation. You should be excited by the idea of taking recurring customer pain and turning it into durable systems: better agents, better documentation, better internal tooling, sharper product feedback, and fewer repeat issues. It is someone with strong technical instincts, a deep user mindset, and a track record of building support systems that change how a team operates. You might be a great fit if you have built an AI-powered support function, owned support tooling at scale, worked deeply with LLMs or automation, or carried a support strategy from problem discovery through implementation and measurement. What you will own Building the AI systems that make support scale You will design, build, and continuously improve the AI-powered systems that help Dust support customers with speed and quality. This includes agents for ticket classification, auto-acknowledgement, response drafting, internal routing, proactive incident detection, knowledge retrieval, and escalation support. You will identify categories of recurring issues and engineer them out of the support queue. Sometimes that means building a better Dust agent. Sometimes it means improving documentation, creating an internal tool, tightening a workflow, writing a script, or escalating product feedback upstream with enough context for engineering to act. You will be expected to measure whether the systems you build actually improve the user experience. Seniority here means not just shipping tooling, but knowing what good looks like, instrumenting it, and iterating until the impact is visible. Running complex support when the systems fall short You will still be close to the work. You will investigate complex customer issues across logs, code, internal tooling, product behavior, and agent outputs. You will provide clear, accurate answers to customers, including when the underlying issue is ambiguous or technically complex. You will handle escalated cases with precision and judgment, communicating clearly with both technical and non-technical users. You should be comfortable translating between customer language, product behavior, engineering detail, and business impact. When AI-generated responses are incomplete, inconsistent, or wrong, you will debug the system behind them. You will improve prompts, knowledge sources, workflows, routing, tooling, and escalation paths so that the same failure mode does not repeat. Shaping the support strategy You will help define how Dust should run support as we scale. That means thinking beyond the queue and owning the full loop: what customers experience, what support sees, what agents can handle, what engineering needs to fix, and what product should learn. You will translate repeated customer pain into high-quality product signal. You will build strong working relationships with engineers and product teams so escalations are high-context, actionable, and efficient. You will also help raise the bar for how the support function operates: what we measure, how we prioritize, how we review quality, how we onboard junior team members, and how we decide what should be automated versus handled by a human. What we are looking for Every candidate and employee’s success at Dust is measured against the same three dimensions: Aptitude, Attitude, and Agency. Aptitude You have strong technical depth. You are comfortable with APIs, web applications, logs, scripts, and internal tools. You can navigate a codebase, reason through product behavior, and troubleshoot systems without being stopped by a stack trace. You have genuine AI fluency at builder level. You have built agents, automations, workflows, or internal tools using AI systems such as Dust, Cursor, Claude Code, n8n, GPT-4, Claude, Mistral, Gemini, or similar platforms. You are not just good at prompting. You understand how to turn AI into operational leverage. You have experience operating at the strategy layer of support, not only at the ticket layer. You have owned or helped shape support systems, support tooling, escalation workflows, deflection strategy, knowledge management, or AI support operations. You can balance technical accuracy with user experience. You care about whether the customer understood the answer, whether the product pain was addressed, and whether the issue will happen again. You are able to communicate bidirectionally: clearly enough for customers, technically enough for engineers, and strategically enough for leadership. Attitude You combine resilience with empathy. This is a front-line role, and customer frustration is often direct and unfiltered. You do not take it personally, but you do take it seriously. You are proactive rather than reactive. You do not wait for a perfect problem statement from the customer. You investigate, infer, clarify, and anticipate what they may need next. You have strong prioritization judgment. You know what needs an immediate human response, what can be automated, what should be escalated, and what should become product feedback. You are comfortable setting boundaries. You do not say yes to everything, and you can explain tradeoffs clearly in a way that builds trust rather than eroding it. You care about the craft of support. You see support as a product experience, not a back-office function. Agency You turn patterns into systems. When you see the same issue twice, you start asking whether it should exist at all. You go deep before escalating. You investigate as far as you reasonably can, so that when you involve engineering or product, they receive a clear problem statement, relevant evidence, and a useful recommendation. You build without waiting for permission. If you see a gap in the support system, you are excited to prototype, test, and ship a better version. You continuously improve your own workflows. description: Senior Data Scientist - Credit Risk Modelling Hybrid in London or remote in the UK We’re looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join our Credit Risk Modelling team. You'll shape how iwoca models credit risk – setting the technical direction on multi-quarter projects, and lifting the bar for the team as you go. The company Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are. That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed. We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive. The team The Credit Risk Modelling team owns credit risk and Customer Lifetime Value (CLtV) modelling for iwoca's UK and German lending. That covers the probabilistic machine learning models behind every credit decision, plus the CLtV models that shape pricing and portfolio strategy. The team is around twelve data scientists. Some work on auto-space models that decide within five minutes from data candidates authorise us to pull. Others work on manual-space models that pick up when a credit analyst adds digital footprint and income data, which lands a decision within 24 hours. The role You'll own credit and CLtV modelling projects end to end, from spotting where the modelling stack is holding the business back through to landing the change. The work spans keeping production models healthy, incremental development, and research that reshapes how the models work. AI has lowered the cost of prototyping enough that ideas which used to sit below the priority line are now viable, so the R&D share of the role is growing. Live examples of the work: Causal estimation of offer terms. Modelling how amount, duration, and price shape customer outcomes. Unifying auto and manual models. The two families were built without forced technical alignment. Finding a principled way to unify them on a common cost function is open work. IFRS accounting model. A multi-stage credit model where information propagates back from later-stage recovery predictions to sharpen upfront loss estimates. Generalising credit and CLtV. Whether a more general framing could replace both separate models is an open research question. The requirements Essential: Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience. Statistical foundations. You have a background in probability and statistics from a quantitative field. You reason about uncertainty and calibration as first-order concerns. Production ML. You have built and shipped supervised ML models end to end – exploration, training, deployment, monitoring. Research mindset. You proactively explore new ways to add value. R&D time is when you expect to find the next step change. Judgement. You critically evaluate model output – yours, a colleague's, or an LLM's – and can explain why a choice is right. You defend your reasoning under challenge, and challenge others' when the evidence points elsewhere. You've influenced technical direction beyond your own projects. Project leadership. You've owned modelling projects end to end, from spotting the opportunity through framing, method choice, shipping, and landing the commercial impact. You move fast, iterate, and update on new evidence rather than chase perfection. AI fluency. You use AI as a primary tool. You prototype with it, automate with it, and take on R&D that would not otherwise be viable. You use judgement on where it helps and where it doesn't. Bonus: Domain experience. You have worked in credit risk, lending, or customer lifetime value modelling. Non-linear methods. You have shipped gradient boosting or neural networks on tabular data in production. Bayesian methods. You have used hierarchical models, MCMC, or Bayesian updating in real work. Time series modelling. You have modelled temporal data where autocorrelation, drift, or seasonality mattered. Python. The stack the team uses. The salary We expect to pay from £90,000 – £120,000 for this role. But, we’re open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews. The culture At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective. We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them. The offices We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work: Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks. Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions. The benefits Flexible working hours. Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership. A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents. 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave. A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years. Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support. 3% Pension contributions on total earnings. An employee equity incentive scheme. Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money. Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme. Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield. And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer: A learning and development budget for everyone. Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers. Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.
